items.title: The Five Kinds of Fruit Named — Karmic Ripening and Consistent Outflow Defined

items.zh: 謂略有五。一者、異熟果，二者、等流果，三者、離繫果，四者、士用果，五者、增上果。諸不善法，於諸惡趣受異熟果；善有漏法，於諸善趣受異熟果；是名異熟果。
items.en: There are, in brief, five: karmic-ripening fruit, consistent-outflow fruit, liberation fruit, effort fruit, and dominant-condition fruit. ... Unwholesome phenomena ripen into the lower realms as karmic-ripening fruit; wholesome yet still contaminated phenomena ripen into the favourable realms as karmic-ripening fruit. This is called karmic-ripening fruit.

items.zh: 習不善故，樂住不善，不善法增。修習善故，樂住善法，善法增長。或似先業，後果隨轉，是名等流果。
items.en: Through habituation to the unwholesome, one comes to dwell contentedly in the unwholesome, and unwholesome tendencies increase. Through cultivating the wholesome, one comes to dwell contentedly in wholesome practice, and wholesome tendencies grow. Or a later result may simply resemble the earlier action that produced it. This is called consistent-outflow fruit.

items.title: Section: Liberation Fruit, and a Caution Against Mistaking Deep Stillness for Genuine Realisation

items.zh: 八支聖道滅諸煩惱，名離繫果。若諸異生，以世俗道滅諸煩惱，不究竟故，非離繫果。
items.en: The eightfold noble path extinguishes affliction — this is called liberation fruit. If an ordinary, unenlightened being suppresses affliction merely through worldly concentration, this is not ultimate, and therefore is not liberation fruit.

items.title: Section: Effort Fruit and Dominant-Condition Fruit — From a Farmer's Harvest to the Twenty-Two Faculties

items.zh: 諸有一類，於現法中，依止隨一工巧業處，起士夫用。所謂農作、商賈、事王、書畫、算數、占卜等事。由此成辦諸稼穡等財利等果，是名士用果。
items.en: Certain people, in this very life, resting on some particular craft, exercise their own skilled effort — farming, trading, serving a ruler, writing or painting, calculation, or divination. Through this, they accomplish the fruit of a harvest, profit, or similar gain. This is called effort fruit.

items.zh: 若眼識等，是眼根增上果；乃至意識等，是意根增上果。眾生身分不散不壞，是命根增上果。二十二根，各各能起自增上果。當知一切名增上果。
items.en: Eye-consciousness and the rest are the dominant-condition fruit of the eye faculty and the corresponding faculties, all the way through mental consciousness as the dominant-condition fruit of the mental faculty. ... Each of the twenty-two faculties gives rise to its own dominant-condition fruit. It should be understood that all of this is called dominant-condition fruit.

items.zh: 二十二根增上作用，如攝事分應知其相。

items.title: Section: The Fruit of Practice — How Understanding Cause and Effect Itself Gradually Purifies and Strengthens

items.zh: 菩薩於是內明所顯正因果相如實知已，精勤修習，令處非處智力種姓漸得清淨、漸得增長。
items.en: Bodhisattvas, having truly understood the genuine cause-and-effect revealed by inner teaching, diligently practice in accordance with it, gradually purifying and gradually strengthening the lineage of the power to discern what is genuinely possible from what is not.

items.zh: 云何內明論顯示已作不失、未作不得相？

items.title: Section: Why Karma Never Simply Vanishes, and Never Simply Appears From Nothing — Closing Inner Teaching's Full Account

items.zh: 謂諸有情自所作業，雖復作已經多百劫，與果功能終無失壞。
items.en: Whatever action beings themselves genuinely perform, even after hundreds of eons have passed since it was done, its capacity to yield its own fruit is never ultimately lost or destroyed.

items.zh: 亦無不作、或復異作，而有異熟、或異果熟。菩薩於是內明所顯已作不失、未作不得相如實知已，精勤修習，令其自業智力種姓漸得清淨、漸得增長。
items.en: Nor is there any case of an action one never performed, or an action performed by someone else, producing a karmic-ripening result for oneself. ... Bodhisattvas, having truly understood this teaching that inner teaching reveals, diligently practice in accordance with it, gradually purifying and strengthening the lineage of the power to know their own and others' karma.

items.title: Section: How to Seek Opens — Walking Burning Iron Ground for a Single Verse

items.zh: 菩薩云何求聞正法？謂諸菩薩於善說法，應當安住猛利愛重，求聞正法。
items.en: How do bodhisattvas seek to hear the true teaching? ... Bodhisattvas, towards a well-spoken teaching, should abide in intense, deeply felt love and respect as they seek to hear the true teaching.

items.zh: 如是略說於善說法安住猛利愛重之相。
謂諸菩薩為欲聽聞一善說法，假使路由猛焰熾然大熱鐵地，無餘方便可得聞是善說法者，即便發起猛利愛重，歡喜而入，何況欲聞多善言義。
items.en: Bodhisattvas, wishing to hear even a single well-spoken teaching, would — if the only path to it crossed ground of blazing, fiercely burning, red-hot iron, with no other means of reaching it — at once give rise to intense love and respect, and enter joyfully; how much more so, then, wishing to hear a teaching rich in extensive meaning.

items.title: Comparing Love of the Teaching Against Everything Else — Five Classical Measures

items.zh: 又諸菩薩於自身分，及於一切資身眾具飲食等事所有愛重，於欲聽聞諸善說法所有愛重；以前愛重方後愛重，於百分中不及其一，於千分中亦不及一，於數分中亦不及一，於算分中亦不及一，乃至鄔波尼殺曇分亦不及一。
items.en: Bodhisattvas' love and regard for their own body, and for all the food, clothing, and requisites that sustain the body, compared against their love and regard for wishing to hear well-spoken teachings — measuring the former love against the latter — does not come within one part in a hundred, nor one part in a thousand, nor one part in any countable number, nor one part in any calculable fraction, not even one part in an uncountably vast fraction.

items.title: Section: Delighting in the Teacher — Never Tired, Never Satisfied, Never Seeking Gain

items.zh: 菩薩如是於善說法深生敬重，常樂聽聞諸善說法，無有勞倦，亦無厭足。
items.en: Bodhisattvas, having in this way given rise to deep reverence for well-spoken teaching, constantly delight in hearing well-spoken teachings, without ever growing weary, and without ever being satisfied.

items.zh: 淨信淳厚，其性柔和，心直見直。愛敬德故、愛敬法故，往法師所無難詰心，有敬重心，無高慢心。專為求善，非顯己德。為欲安立自他善根，不為利養恭敬因緣。
items.en: Pure faith, deep and unwavering, a nature that is gentle, a mind and outlook that run straight towards the truth. Because they love and respect the teacher's virtue, and love and respect the teaching itself, they approach the teacher without any argumentative intent, holding a respectful mind, free of any arrogant mind. Their purpose is solely to seek what is good, never to display their own virtue. They act only to establish roots of goodness in themselves and others, never for the sake of gain or being honoured.

items.zh: 菩薩具足如是功德，往法師所，無雜染心、無散亂心聽聞正法。云何菩薩無雜染心聽聞正法？

items.title: Section: Hearing Without a Defiled Mind — Eleven Marks Across Three Defilements

items.zh: 謂聽法時，其心遠離貢高雜染，其心遠離輕慢雜染，其心遠離怯弱雜染。由六種相，其心遠離貢高雜染；由四種相，其心遠離輕慢雜染；由一種相，其心遠離怯弱雜染。
items.en: When hearing the teaching, the mind should be free of the defilement of pride, free of the defilement of contempt, and free of the defilement of cowardly inadequacy. Through six marks, the mind is freed of the defilement of pride; through four marks, the mind is freed of the defilement of contempt; through one mark, the mind is freed of the defilement of cowardly inadequacy.

items.zh: 謂聽法時，應時而聽、慇重而聽、恭敬而聽、不為損害、不為隨順、不求過失。由此六相，其心遠離貢高雜染。又聽法時，恭敬正法、恭敬說法補特伽羅、不輕正法、不輕說法補特伽羅。由此四相，其心遠離輕慢雜染。又聽法時，不自輕
items.en: When hearing the teaching: listening at the fitting time, listening earnestly, listening respectfully, not obstructing the teacher, not merely going along without asking, and not seeking out the teacher's faults. ... And when hearing the teaching: respecting the true teaching, respecting the person who teaches it, not belittling the true teaching, and not belittling the person who teaches it. ... And when hearing the teaching: not belittling oneself.

items.zh: 蔑。由此一相，其心遠離怯弱雜染。菩薩如是無雜染心聽聞正法。云何菩薩無散亂心聽聞正法？謂由五相。一者、求悟解心聽聞正法，二者、專一趣心聽聞正法，三者、聆音屬耳聽聞正法，四者、掃滌其心聽聞正法，

blocks.text: Five kinds of fruit, then how a bodhisattva seeks to hear the Dharma, with one of the treatise's most vivid images. A short passage (0502a24 area) is untranslated.

**Karmic ripening**: "unwholesome actions ripen in the lower destinies; wholesome contaminated actions, in good ones". **Consistent outflow**: "through habituating the unwholesome, one delights in it and it grows"; likewise the wholesome. **Liberation** (separation): "the noble eightfold path's extinguishing of afflictions". Suppressing affliction by worldly concentration "is not ultimate". **Effort**: what one achieves by a craft: farming, trade, writing. **Dominant condition**: eye-consciousness is the fruit of the eye faculty, and so on.

"Whatever action beings genuinely perform, even after hundreds of aeons, its capacity to yield fruit is never lost. Nor does an action one never performed, or one performed by another, ripen for oneself."

"Bodhisattvas, wishing to hear even a single well-spoken teaching, would, if the only path to it crossed ground of blazing red-hot iron, at once set out." Their love for the Dharma surpasses their love for body and wealth: "not one-hundredth" compares.

They "constantly delight in hearing, never weary, never satisfied", with "pure faith, a gentle nature, a mind straight towards the truth". Master Cháng Bǎi: a big tree does not fall in the wind, as a small one does in a typhoon. Venerable Miào Jìng: like a great rock unmoved by strong wind.

"Free of the defilement of pride, of contempt, and of timidity." One listens "at the fitting time, earnestly, respectfully, not obstructing the teacher, not merely going along without asking, not seeking the teacher's faults". Master Cháng Bǎi: coming to check whether the teacher is right, as if one's own wisdom were already enough, is arrogance.

quiz.q: "Wholesome contaminated actions yield ripening in good destinies." What is the nature of the ripening fruit, per Master Cháng Bǎi?
options: the cause may be good or bad; the fruit is only neutral — also called retribution fruit
quiz.why: "Unwholesome actions yield karmic ripening in the lower destinies; wholesome contaminated actions yield it in the good destinies — this is called ripening fruit." Master Cháng Bǎi: "the cause spans good and bad; the fruit is only neutral" — ripening fruit is only neutral; it's also called retribution fruit.

quiz.q: "Later results resembling prior deeds — consistent outflow." What example does Venerable Miào Jìng give?
options: why does someone love medicine? He was a doctor in a past life — consistent outflow
quiz.why: "Through habituating unwholesomeness, one delights in it and it grows … or later results follow along resembling prior deeds — this is called consistent-outflow fruit." Venerable Miào Jìng: why does he delight in this? He was also a doctor in a past life — so it's consistent outflow.

quiz.q: "Ordinary beings extinguishing afflictions by worldly paths — not ultimate, not the fruit of separation." What do the masters say?
options: Cháng Bǎi: only temporarily suppressed, like a stone on grass, seeds intact; Miào Jìng: contemplating impurity can't extinguish affliction but strongly subdues desire
it is the fruit of separation
quiz.why: "The noble eightfold path's extinguishing of afflictions is called the fruit of separation. Ordinary beings extinguishing afflictions by worldly paths — since it isn't ultimate, it isn't the fruit of separation." Master Cháng Bǎi: it's only temporary suppression, like a stone pressing grass; the seeds aren't cut, they just don't manifest. Venerable Miào Jìng: contemplating impurity can't extinguish affliction, but it has great power to subdue desire.

quiz.q: "Eye-consciousness is the dominant-condition fruit of the eye faculty." How does Master Cháng Bǎi explain?
options: the eye faculty is the dominant condition producing eye-consciousness — so the latter is its fruit
quiz.why: "Eye-consciousness and the like are the dominant-condition fruit of the eye faculty; up to mind-consciousness, of the mind faculty." Master Cháng Bǎi: the eye faculty is the dominant condition producing eye-consciousness, so eye-consciousness is its dominant-condition fruit.

quiz.q: "No ripening without doing, or from 異作" — rendered "a different action." How do the lectures read 異作?
options: Cháng Bǎi: another does the deed and you reap it — impossible; Miào Jìng: what you didn't do yourself brings you no merit
quiz.why: "Nor is there ripening or a ripened fruit without the action having been done, or with it done by another." Master Cháng Bǎi: someone else creates karma and you receive its ripening — that never happens. Venerable Miào Jìng: by Buddhist teaching, what you didn't do yourself — you don't get its merit. The English "different action" misses "done by another."

quiz.q: "To hear a single well-spoken teaching" — how little, per Master Cháng Bǎi?
options: as little as a single four-line verse
quiz.why: "Bodhisattvas, wishing to hear a single well-spoken teaching, even if the road lay across ground of blazing red-hot iron … would gladly enter." Master Cháng Bǎi: down to even a single four-line verse — that's "a single well-spoken teaching."

quiz.q: Listening "free of the defilement of arrogance." How does Master Cháng Bǎi describe arrogance?
options: thinking one's wisdom suffices and coming to check whether the teacher is right
quiz.why: "When listening, the mind is free of the defilement of arrogance, of contempt, and of timidity." Master Cháng Bǎi: don't think your wisdom is already enough and come to see whether the teacher is right — that's arrogance.
